FaultDeck Desktop UI — Design ​

Date: 2026-11-08 · Status: approved for implementation · Shell: Tauri (Rust + WebView)

1. Decision ​

Tauri 2 desktop shell (native window + WebView), Rust backend calls the FaultDeck coordinator directly over the existing TCP wire protocol — no extra HTTP layer, no Node bridge. Chosen over Electron (smaller, Rust-native, no Node) and over a pure web dashboard (no installer — the user requires setup.exe/dmg installers in the nightly matrix).

Linux build deps confirmed present: webkit2gtk-4.1 (2.52.6), gtk+-3.0 (3.24.52), node 24 / pnpm 12.

2. Architecture ​

faultdeck-desktop/  (Tauri app, added to the workspace as a crate)
  src-tauri/  (Rust): tauri commands -> coordinator wire client
      └ coordinator.rs   # TcpStream client speaking WireMessage/AgentCommand
  ui/         (frontend, pnpm + Vite + vanilla TS)
      └ src/  views + a tiny wire-client (fetch -> tauri invoke)

The Rust side is the only thing that talks to the coordinator. The frontend calls invoke("coordinator_list") / invoke("coordinator_inject", …) / invoke("coordinator_rollback", …); those run in Rust, open a TCP stream, send the JSON wire message, await the framed response.

3. Wire contract (verbatim from crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs) ​

Every request is one WireMessage line, newline-framed, UTF-8 JSON:

json
{"token":"<optional>","command":{"cmd":"list_agents"}}
{"token":"<optional>","command":{"cmd":"inject","id":"<agent_id>","injection":{"fault":{"kind":"latency","milliseconds":100},"target":{"source":null,"destination":"10.0.0.0/24","destination_port":9000}}}}
{"token":"<optional>","command":{"cmd":"rollback","id":"<agent_id>"}}
{"token":"<optional>,"command":{"cmd":"fetch_report","id":"<agent_id>","scenario_hash":"<hash>"}}

Responses are AgentResponse tagged on status: ok | error | registered | queued | agents{agents,available} | report{report}.

The agents response drives the fleet view: { "agents":[{"id","capabilities","last_seen_ms","online"}], "available":[...] }.

The report response carries a RunReport: {scenario_name, scenario_yaml, scenario_hash, injected_at_ms, rolled_back_at_ms, events[], restore_evidence[], external_assertions[], replay_command}.

Fault spec shapes (serde tag kind): latency{milliseconds}, loss{percent}, disconnect{all_traffic}. Target: {source?, destination?, destination_port?} (IpNet strings).

4. Views ​

4.1 Fleet (default) ​

  • Card per agent: id, online dot, capabilities chips, last_seen.
  • Header: coordinator host/port (editable), token (optional), Connect, Refresh.
  • Per-card actions: Inject (opens 4.2), Rollback (confirm; disabled when nothing applied).
  • Applied-fault badge: agent id → scenario hash from applied state (shown when known).

4.2 Inject dialog ​

  • Fault kind segmented control: Latency / Loss / Disconnect.
    • Latency: milliseconds (1..86,400,000).
    • Loss: percent (0 < p ≤ 100).
    • Disconnect: all_traffic toggle.
  • Target: source (optional IpNet), destination (optional IpNet), destination_port (optional 1..65535). At least one of destination / destination_port required (UI validation).
  • Apply sends inject; shows the agent response (ok / queued / error).

4.3 Report ​

  • List of archived reports (scenario_hash → title), latest first.
  • Selected report: scenario YAML (monospace), injected/rolled-back timestamps, event timeline, restore-evidence table (check/passed/detail), external assertions (pass/fail), replay command with a Copy button.

4.4 Settings (persisted in localStorage) ​

  • Coordinator host/port, token, heartbeat timeout.

5. Error & edge handling ​

  • Coordinator unreachable: inline banner "coordinator unreachable at host:port" + retry; never a blank screen.
  • Empty fleet: empty-state panel "no agents registered — start faultdeck-agent on the target and it appears here."
  • Inject validation errors render under the field; the backend error response renders in the dialog footer.
  • Long-running dispatch shows a spinner; results land in the event timeline.

6. Acceptance ​

  1. cargo build -p faultdeck-desktop green; tauri build produces the platform installer.
  2. Against a live coordinator + one agent: connect → agent appears online → inject latency → applied badge → rollback → badge clears.
  3. Report list loads a real RunReport; replay command copies.
  4. All above exercised in the headless check (coordinator + agent on 127.0.0.1 ephemeral ports) as part of the nightly CI smoke.
